original_question: An uphill lattice path is a doubly infinite monotone path in R^2 made of unit steps from (a, b) to either (a, b + 1) or (a + 1, b), and a downhill lattice path is defined similarly with b - 1 in place of b + 1. For a finite set P of points in Z^2, call such a monotone lattice path friendly if the number of points of P on one side of the path equals the number on the other side, ignoring points that lie on the path itself. Is it true that every odd-sized finite set of lattice points has a friendly path?
target_in_paper: Section 5, Problem 8, “Friendly paths,” where the paper reproduces the author’s American Mathematical Monthly Problem 11484.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s official formulation. It correctly uses a finite set P ⊂ Z^2, doubly infinite uphill/downhill lattice paths built from unit horizontal/vertical steps, the rule that points of P lying on the path are ignored, and the existence question for odd-cardinality point sets.
missing_details: The paper defines an uphill lattice path as the union of a doubly infinite sequence of directed line segments in R^2, each joining an integer pair to an adjacent pair via either (a,b)→(a+1,b) or (a,b)→(a,b+1).
A downhill lattice path is defined with allowed steps (a,b)→(a+1,b) or (a,b)→(a,b-1); this should be stated explicitly rather than only by analogy.
The paper explicitly defines a monotone lattice path to mean either an uphill lattice path or a downhill lattice path.
To make the question fully stand-alone, “on one side of the path” should be formalized as the two connected components of R^2 \ gamma determined by the doubly infinite monotone path gamma.
refined_question: Let P be a finite subset of Z^2 with |P| odd. An uphill lattice path is the union gamma of a doubly infinite sequence of directed unit line segments in R^2, each joining a lattice point (a,b) to either (a+1,b) or (a,b+1). A downhill lattice path is defined similarly, except that the allowed steps are (a,b)→(a+1,b) and (a,b)→(a,b-1). A monotone lattice path is either uphill or downhill. Call gamma friendly for P if, after discarding the points of P that lie on gamma, the two connected components of R^2 \ gamma contain the same number of points of P. Is it true that every finite set P ⊂ Z^2 of odd cardinality admits a friendly monotone lattice path?
justification: The nearest official target is exactly Section 5, Problem 8. The paper gives the path definitions immediately before posing the question, and it does not broaden this item into a more general conjectural program or supply an equivalent reformulation. Your draft already matches the substance of the paper almost verbatim; the only needed sharpening is to import the exact step-by-step definition of uphill/downhill paths and to make the phrase “one side of the path” precise.
